summary: The enterprise AI model API landscape in 2026 is dominated by the three hyperscalers—AWS Bedrock, Azure OpenAI/Foundry, and Google Vertex AI—each offering managed access to multiple foundation models within the customer's own cloud security perimeter. Data-platform players (Snowflake Cortex AI, Databricks) and specialized vendors (IBM watsonx, Oracle, Cloudflare) compete by bringing models to where enterprise data already lives. There is no single winner; the best fit is driven primarily by an organization's existing cloud footprint, compliance requirements, and the breadth of model choice needed.
why_enterprises_use_aggregators: Data residency and privacy: inference runs inside the enterprise's own cloud VPC/tenant so prompts and outputs never leave the governed environment or train vendor models.

Compliance and governance: aggregators inherit the cloud provider's certifications (SOC 2, HIPAA, ISO 27001, FedRAMP, GDPR) and provide centralized audit logging, identity, and access controls (IAM, Entra ID).
Single billing and existing contracts: consumption flows through established cloud enterprise agreements and committed-spend discounts rather than dozens of separate vendor invoices.
Model choice and portability: one API and SDK unlocks many models (Claude, Llama, Mistral, Gemini, GPT, Nova, etc.), reducing lock-in and letting teams swap models without re-architecting.
Enterprise integration and security: native VPC networking, private endpoints, key management, fine-tuning/RAG tooling, and content safety filters integrate with the rest of the cloud stack.

platforms.name: Azure OpenAI Service (Azure AI Foundry)
platforms.pricing: Pay-as-you-go per 1K/1M tokens (input/output) plus Provisioned Throughput Units (PTUs) for reserved capacity; billed through Azure Enterprise Agreement.
key_features: Private VNet integration and private endpoints
Data not used to train base models
platforms.best_for: Microsoft-first enterprises wanting the latest OpenAI models with deep Azure and Microsoft 365 integration.

platforms.name: AWS Bedrock
platforms.pricing: On-demand per-token pricing plus Provisioned Throughput for reserved capacity; also Batch and model-specific rates, billed through AWS accounts.
key_features: Data not retained or used for training
platforms.best_for: AWS-centric enterprises wanting the widest choice of models (especially Claude) behind a single API.

platforms.name: Google Vertex AI Model Garden
platforms.pricing: Pay-per-token for most models plus Generative AI Scale Units (GSUs) for reserved provisioned throughput (e.g., 25 GSUs of Gemini 2.5 Flash ≈ 67,250 tokens/sec); billed through Google Cloud.
key_features: VPC Service Controls and private endpoints
Model Garden with first- and third-party models
Data not used to train base models
platforms.best_for: Google Cloud customers and teams wanting Gemini's long context, multimodal capabilities, and tight data/analytics integration.

platforms.name: Snowflake Cortex AI
platforms.pricing: Consumption-based using Snowflake credits per token/function call; billed through existing Snowflake contract.
key_features: Models run inside the Snowflake governance boundary
No data movement out of the data cloud
platforms.best_for: Organizations that want to run LLMs directly against governed data already sitting in Snowflake without moving it.

platforms.name: IBM watsonx.ai
platforms.pricing: Resource Unit (RU) consumption-based pricing plus subscription tiers; available as SaaS, on-prem, or hybrid.
key_features: watsonx.governance for model risk and audit
watsonx Orchestrate for multi-platform agent management
platforms.best_for: Regulated industries and hybrid/on-prem shops needing strong AI governance, agent management, and data sovereignty.

platforms.name: Databricks Mosaic AI (Foundation Model APIs)
platforms.pricing: Consumption via Databricks Units (DBUs), pay-per-token or provisioned throughput; billed through Databricks/cloud contract.
platforms.best_for: Data-engineering and ML teams building custom and RAG applications on top of the lakehouse with strong governance.

platforms.name: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) Generative AI
platforms.pricing: Pay-per-character/token on-demand plus dedicated AI clusters for reserved capacity; billed through OCI.
platforms.best_for: Oracle application and database customers wanting generative AI embedded in Fusion apps with sovereign-cloud options.

platforms.name: Cloudflare Workers AI
platforms.pricing: Pay-per-neuron / per-request serverless pricing with a free tier; billed through Cloudflare.
key_features: Serverless edge inference close to users
AI Gateway for caching, rate limiting and observability
platforms.best_for: Developers and enterprises needing low-latency, globally distributed inference on open models at the edge.
